item.title: Hermitian K-theory for stable $\infty$-categories IV: Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.13248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In analogy with the passage from connective to non-connective algebraic K-theory, Schlichting put forward the Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt spectrum as an approximation to Grothendieck-Witt theory by a functor invariant under idempotent completion. In this paper, we extend his construction to the setting of Poincar\'e $\infty$-categories and characterise the resulting functor by the expected universal property. Our main result places these Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt-spectra in an exact sequence involving the ultimately decorated L-spectrum and homotopy orbits of non-connective K-theory. This confirms a conjecture of Williams which had remained open even for rings in which $2$ is invertible, and allows us to deduce universal characterisations for ultimately decorated L-theory. We obtain these results by unifying the Bass-Heller-Swan and Ranicki-Shaneson splittings into a general decomposition theorem that yields, in particular, formulas for Grothendieck-Witt groups of Laurent polynomial rings. Finally, we construct multiplicative structures on both versions of our Grothendieck-Witt and L-functors and refine their universal properties to multiplicative ones. Along the way, we show that the original versions are even idempotent with respect to Day convolution.
item.dc:creator: Baptiste Calm\`es, Emanuele Dotto, Yonatan Harpaz, Fabian Hebestreit, Markus Land, Kristian Moi, Denis Nardin, Thomas Nikolaus, Wolfgang Steimle

item.title: An Equivariant Coarse Green-Julg Theorem for Proper Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove an equivariant coarse Green--Julg theorem for proper isometric actions of countable discrete groups on bounded geometry metric spaces. We introduce the $(\Gamma, X)$-controlled proper $C^{*}$-algebra, and show that the evaluation-at-zero map between the equivariant localization and Roe algebras with such coefficients induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Qin Wang, Chen Zhang

item.title: Algebraic K-theory of geometric fields: rigidity
item.description: arXiv:1309.6045v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of Galois descent for suitably completed algebraic K-theory of fields. One of the main results in the present paper is a suitable form of rigidity for Borel-style generalized equivariant cohomology with respect to certain spectra, which includes mod-${\ell}$ Algebraic K-theory, for $\ell$ -invertible in the base field. Such a rigidity theorem in fact provides a determination of the mod-$\ell$ Algebraic K-theory of geometric fields, i.e., fields that contain an algebraically closed sub-field in terms of the absolute Galois group of the bigger field and proves one conjecture due to the first author. What remains in a proof of a related conjecture of the first author (see [C13]) is a derived completion theorem for equivariant algebraic K-theory with respect to the action of profinite groups. Such a derived completion theorem, with certain restrictions, is proven in the paper, [CJ26-2]. What we do in the remaining part of this paper is to provide a comparison of the generalized Borel style equivariant K-theory considered in [CJ26-2] and also in [C13], with the generalized Borel style equivariant K-theory defined using more standard models of geometric classifying spaces. This enables us to apply the rigidity results proven in this paper to the generalized Borel style equivariant K-theory considered in [CJ26-2], thereby enabling us to provide an affirmative solution to the above mentioned conjecture in many cases.
item.dc:creator: Gunnar Carlsson, Roy Joshua
